boss_stat.description: Per-era boss stats (ported from the prototype's live py-only BOSS_ERAS; its swarm_* fields were dead and are not migrated). BR-1: EVERY boss variable is per-era, so footprint, sprite_scale and shake live in this row too -- the Boss is the ONE type whose render fit is era-indexed (every other type keeps them flat at its root, D10).

dmg.description: Boss damage per hit (x10 combat scale, D-12).

footprint.description: This era's boss tile footprint: it occupies footprint x footprint tiles. Drives BOTH the render fit (its sprite is downscaled to footprint*tile_w wide, never upscaled) and ER-2 clearance pathing. Per-era since BR-1, so a later boss can be physically bigger than an early one.

hp.description: Boss hit points (x10 combat scale, D-12).

move_speed.description: Boss movement speed in tiles per second.

name.description: Boss display name for this era (used by the boss announcement).

shake.description: Screen shake while THIS era's boss walks (per-era since BR-1).

sprite_scale.description: Extra render multiplier applied AFTER this era's footprint fit (1.0 = fit exactly). The deliberate knob for low-res art, which is never auto-upscaled; may exceed 1.

condition_path_weights.description: This type's own terrain path-cost weights (per-enemy-type override of the base pathfinder weights). DUPLICATES map.json's TileConditions.path_weights and will NOT track future changes to it -- there is deliberately no nullable "inherit" sentinel, because editor/panels/balancing.py reads prop.get("type") and a type-less schema node raises "no widget for schema", crashing the balancing panel for the whole enemies domain. Same bounds policy as Pathfinding.content_weights in map.json.

forest.description: Extra path weight of a forest tile for this enemy type.

mountain.description: Extra path weight of a mountain tile for this enemy type.

pond.description: Extra path weight of a pond tile for this enemy type.

death_spawn.description: Optional-mechanic block (ER-3, D4): when this unit's HP falls to or below at_hp_fraction of its max it DIES (one code path - breaking formation is dying) and, if enabled, bursts the spawns row for its era at the tile it died on. at_hp_fraction 0.0 + enabled false is an inert unit that dies at zero HP and leaves nothing.

at_hp_fraction.description: Death threshold as a fraction of max HP: the unit dies when hp <= max_hp * this. 0.0 = the normal die-at-zero rule. 0.5 = a formation that scatters at half health. Values at or above 1.0 kill the unit the instant it spawns - do not.

enabled.description: Toggle: false means this unit dies at its at_hp_fraction threshold but spawns nothing.

spawn_hp_fraction.description: Children spawn at this fraction of their OWN max HP. 1.0 = full health (the Boss's 10G swarm). Keep it above every child type's own at_hp_fraction or the children die on the frame they appear.

spawns.description: What this unit bursts into, ONE ROW PER ERA, index-aligned with the type's era table (the Boss's stats/round_counts). A type with no eras carries a single row; the era index clamps into the array, so row 0 always applies. This is the era table and the flat per-type table in one shape - there is deliberately no union here.

pacing_endgame_scaling.description: How wave pacing keeps moving past the last authored EnemyScaling era row. All factors ship 1.0.

batch_size.description: Compounding multiplier applied once per era past the last authored era row: last_row_value * factor**N. 1.0 = plain clamp (what ships today, behaviour-neutral). Applied to batch_size (floored to a whole number of enemies).

spawn_interval.description: Compounding multiplier applied once per era past the last authored era row: last_row_value * factor**N. 1.0 = plain clamp (what ships today, behaviour-neutral). Applied to spawn_interval.

pacing_era_row.description: Wave pacing for one era. Era N of the global era clock (EnemyScaling.rounds_per_era) reads row N; past the last authored row the values clamp to it and the matching endgame_scaling factors compound (value * factor**N).

batch_size.description: How many queued enemies ONE spawn-timer expiry releases at once. 1 = one at a time. This only bunches the wave: a round's totals are unchanged by it.

spawn_interval.description: Seconds between spawn events within a wave in this era (the ramp and the per-spawn jitter still apply on top).

spawn_counts.description: A mix of enemy counts by type. SHARED by every death_spawn.spawns row and by Boss.round_counts, so a key added here appears on all of them (BR-1/D3 accepted that cost for commander, deliberately overriding the standing argument against widening this $def).

commander.description: Commander count. Ships 0 everywhere: the Commander enemy type itself arrives in BR-2 and nothing spawns it yet.

type_endgame_scaling.description: How this type keeps growing past its last authored era row, instead of freezing forever. All factors ship 1.0.

count.description: Compounding multiplier applied once per era past the last authored era row: last_row_value * factor**N. 1.0 = plain clamp (what ships today, behaviour-neutral). Applied to count_start and count_per_round; resolved counts are floored to whole enemies.

dmg.description: Compounding multiplier applied once per era past the last authored era row: last_row_value * factor**N. 1.0 = plain clamp (what ships today, behaviour-neutral). Applied to dmg.

hp.description: Compounding multiplier applied once per era past the last authored era row: last_row_value * factor**N. 1.0 = plain clamp (what ships today, behaviour-neutral). Applied to hp.

move_speed.description: Compounding multiplier applied once per era past the last authored era row: last_row_value * factor**N. 1.0 = plain clamp (what ships today, behaviour-neutral). Applied to move_speed.

type_era_row.description: One era's fully manual stats and count schedule for an enemy type. Stats are absolute values, NOT bonuses added to a base. Era N of the global era clock (EnemyScaling.rounds_per_era) reads row N; past the last authored row the values clamp to it and the matching endgame_scaling factors compound (value * factor**N).

count_per_round.description: Extra spawns of this type added per round after r0. Fractional is meaningful: 1/3 = one more every three rounds.

count_start.description: How many of this type spawn on the era's first ACTIVE round, r0 = max(the era's first round, start_round). A NUMBER, not an integer: the resolver floors count_start + k * count_per_round, so a fractional anchor is what makes an accretion schedule (one more every three rounds) survive an era boundary exactly. Authoring a fresh era, type a whole number.

per_round.description: Flat additive stat growth per round WITHIN this era: stats + (round_in_era - 1) * per_round. All zero = stats step once per era and sit flat between steps. attack_speed and attack_range_tiles deliberately have no in-era growth.

dmg.description: Damage added per round within the era (x10 combat scale, D-12). 0 = flat.

hp.description: Hit points added per round within the era (x10 combat scale, D-12). 0 = flat.

move_speed.description: Move speed added per round within the era, in tiles per second. 0 = flat.

stats.description: This type's absolute combat stats on the era's FIRST round (per_round grows them from there).

dmg.description: Damage per hit (x10 combat scale, D-12).

move_speed.description: Movement speed in tiles per second.

description: Enemies balancing domain (D-10), REPLAN nested tree (Phase 9A). Values are the prototype's live tuning, verbatim. HP/DMG use the x10 combat scale (D-12). Bounds policy: fractions 0-1, HP/DMG 0-100000, costs/counts 0-10000, rounds/levels 0-1000, seconds 0-60, pixels 1-4096; footprint tiles 1-8; sprite_scale multiplier 0.1-8.

EnemyScaling.description: The global era clock and per-era wave pacing. One clock drives enemy scaling AND the boss round: era = (round - 1) // rounds_per_era, round_in_era = (round - 1) % rounds_per_era + 1, and a round is a boss round iff round_in_era == boss_round_in_era. Round 0 (the tutorial) is era 0 and is never a boss round.

boss_round_in_era.description: Which round WITHIN an era is the boss round, 1..rounds_per_era (rounds_per_era itself = the era's last round, the shipped value).

eras.description: Per-era wave pacing, one row per era, era 0 first. Variable length: add a row for another era, and past the last row endgame_scaling compounds.

rounds_per_era.description: Length of one era in rounds - THE global clock every enemy type and the boss round share.

spawn_ramp_enabled.description: If true each spawn interval is jittered by 1 +/- spawn_ramp_range.

spawn_ramp_range.description: Jitter half-range: intervals vary between (1-range)x and (1+range)x.

tutorial_round_enemy_count.description: The tutorial's round 0 always spawns exactly this many Standard/walker enemies, ignoring base_enemy_count/enemies_per_round/scale-tier formulas entirely. Unused once round_num >= 1.

Boss.description: The boss (on the era's boss_round_in_era round). Per-era arrays are index-aligned with the global era clock: era N uses stats[N], death_spawn.spawns[N], round_counts[N]. BR-1: footprint/sprite_scale/shake moved OUT of this block into the stats rows, so every boss variable is per-era -- the Boss is the one type whose render fit is era-indexed rather than flat at the type root.

hunts.description: What this type paths toward on spawn (Art/prey-hunting). "base" walks straight at the hole, attacking whatever blocks it en route -- the original, unchanged behaviour. "economic"/"defence" hunt the nearest alive building of that category, chosen by geometric distance and routed by weighted cost (find_path_to_nearest_economic/_defence). "any_non_base" (the Boss) hunts the nearest alive non-base building of ANY kind, the hole strictly last. Every value except "base" arms PathAgent.repath_on_kill, so the unit re-targets when its victim dies.

kidnapping.description: If true, this type's killing blow on a building carries it home instead of the enemy walking on: the enemy retags to "kidnapper", counts as dead for scoring, hoists the building's sprite and walks to the nearest spawn tile, and the building's tile is freed for good (no payday revive).

registry_group.description: The data/slots.json enemies group label this type's sprites live under (editor-side link, fix-editor-preview-footprint): NOT always the same string as this EnemyTypes key (e.g. Standard -> "Walker", SiegeCannon -> "Siege Cannon") — must be matched by this field, never by string convention.

stats.description: Per-era boss combat stats -- since BR-1 this row carries EVERY boss variable, including footprint, sprite_scale and shake (which used to be single global values shared by all five bosses).

Commander.description: The Commander (BossReworkPLAN D8/BR-2). A building-hunting officer, sized like a walker but with a boss's toughness -- the era-0 boss's second-phase spawn (BR-3). A NORMAL era-shaped type: its stats resolve through the same base per-era resolver as Standard/SiegeCannon, and footprint/sprite_scale stay FLAT at this root (only the Boss carries them per-era, BR-1/D10). It ships DORMANT: every era row's count_start and count_per_round are 0, so it never enters a normal wave -- but every schedule key exists, so switching it on is a data edit alone.

eras.description: This type's stats and count schedule, one row per era, era 0 first. Variable length: add a row for another era, and past the last row endgame_scaling compounds.

start_round.description: First round commanders appear. 0 with the shipped all-zero era counts means the schedule is armed but emits nothing (BR-2 keeps the type dormant).

Formation.description: A marching column of soldiers that moves as one 2x2 body (ER-4). It breaks at half health - death_spawn.at_hp_fraction 0.5 means it DIES at 50% HP (D4: breaking formation is dying) and scatters its spawns row of regulars at spawn_hp_fraction of their own max HP. Takes the scale-tier bonuses like Standard/SiegeCannon. Never spawns on a boss round (Boss.round_counts carries no formation key, deliberately).
